ballots.name: Priya
ballots.reason: The cached one-minute runtime clears my CI-penalty concern, the two-week advisory trial with a strict rule set and baseline mode addresses the noise risk, and Elena's secret-detection carve-out means the gate catches real bugs from day one—exactly the guardrails I asked for in round one.

ballots.name: Marcus
ballots.reason: The cached one-minute runtime with parallel execution clears my ninety-second threshold, and the two-week advisory trial with cache hit/miss instrumentation gives me the measured data I need before we flip to a hard gate—if cache hits drop below eighty percent, I pull support, but that safeguard is built into the plan.

ballots.name: Elena
ballots.reason: Lintwise's secret-detection rule set closes a real gap—last quarter's leaked test key would have been caught pre-merge—and with the cached one-minute runtime, parallel execution, and my carve-out that secret rules stay hard-fail from day one, the gate protects credentials without slowing the pipeline.

ballots.name: Tom
ballots.reason: The two-week advisory trial, parallel execution with the cached one-minute runtime, Lars's strict rule set with baseline mode, and Elena's secret-detection carve-out address every concern I raised, and I'm ready to tune the JavaScript rules during the window and report back the actionable ratio.

ballots.name: Sana
ballots.reason: The cached one-minute runtime, parallel execution, and two-week advisory trial resolve my latency and pilot concerns, and I'll validate SQL coverage during that window—if Lintwise skips SQL, I'll add a separate linter without blocking the rest of the team.

ballots.name: Lars
ballots.reason: The 8-percent false-positive rate with tuned rules plus baseline mode clears my noise bar, and Jin's phased promotion with per-language reporting and a one-maintainer rollback path protects the signal-to-noise ratio I need to trust our gates.

ballots.name: Jin
ballots.reason: The phased rollout, secret-rule carve-out, parallel execution, strict rule set with baseline mode, and the one-maintainer rollback path I drafted into the merge-policy amendment collectively address every risk I raised, so I can sign the amendment this week.

ballots.name: Olga
ballots.reason: The advisory trial, Tom's onboarding doc with concrete fixes, Lars's baseline mode so I'm not punished for pre-existing debt, and Jin's phased promotion together turn this gate into a teacher rather than a trap, which is exactly what I need as someone still learning our conventions.
